title: What Happens Inside an AI When You Hit Enter?
description:
You type a question, press Enter, and an AI starts answering. This animated explainer follows a single prompt through a large language model: tokenization, embeddings, positional information, transformer layers, attention, feed-forward networks, next-token prediction, sampling with temperature, and the generation loop that streams the answer word by word.

Numbers shown on screen (token IDs, probabilities, layer counts) are illustrative.

scenes.title: Intro
lines: You type a question, press Enter, and a moment later an AI starts answering.
But what actually happens inside, in that one second?
Let's follow a single prompt all the way through.

scenes.title: The prompt
lines: Here's our prompt: Why is the sky blue?
To you, that's a sentence. To the model, it isn't even text yet.

scenes.title: 1. Tokenization
lines: First, a tokenizer chops the text into small pieces called tokens.
A token can be a whole word, part of a word, or even just a space and a question mark.
Each token is swapped for a number: its ID in a vocabulary of around a hundred thousand pieces.

scenes.title: 2. Embeddings
lines: Numbers alone don't carry meaning, so each ID is turned into an embedding.
That's a long list of numbers, thousands of them, that places the token in a kind of meaning space.
Words with similar meanings end up close together, like sky, cloud, and ocean.

scenes.title: 3. Word order
lines: The model also adds information about position.
Dog bites man, and man bites dog, use exactly the same words, but they mean very different things.

scenes.title: 4. Transformer layers
lines: Now the real work begins. The vectors flow up through a tall stack of layers, called transformer blocks.
Large models have dozens of them, sometimes more than a hundred.
And every block does two things: attention, and a feed-forward step.

scenes.title: 5. Attention
lines: Attention lets every token look at every other token, and decide which ones matter.
When the model processes the word blue, it pays strong attention to sky, because that's what blue is describing.
Many attention heads run in parallel, each one tracking a different kind of relationship.

scenes.title: 6. Feed-forward
lines: Then a feed-forward network processes each token on its own, mixing in facts and patterns learned during training.
Layer by layer, the vectors go from raw words to rich understanding: this is a question, about physics, about light and the atmosphere.

scenes.title: 7. Predicting the next token
lines: At the very top, the final vector is turned into a score for every token in the vocabulary.
Those scores become probabilities. Which token is most likely to come next?
Here, The is on top, followed by Because, and Sunlight.

scenes.title: 8. Sampling & temperature
lines: The model then picks one token from this distribution.
A setting called temperature controls how adventurous that choice is. Low temperature plays it safe. Higher temperature gets more creative.

scenes.title: 9. One token at a time
lines: And here's the key idea: the model only ever predicts one token at a time.
The new token is added to the end of the input, and the whole process runs again, and again, and again.
That's why answers appear word by word, streaming onto your screen.

scenes.title: 10. Stopping
lines: Generation stops when the model produces a special end token, or hits a length limit.
The tokens are turned back into text, and you see the finished answer.

scenes.title: Recap
lines: So, in about a second: text became tokens, tokens became vectors, attention and layers built up meaning, and the model predicted the answer, one token at a time.
That's what happens, every time you hit Enter.
